value: An urban lease contract must be made in writing; if the lack of writing is not the tenant's fault, the tenant may prove the lease by showing use of the premises without objection and monthly payment of rent for six months (Art. 1069).
source_publisher: Diário da República (consolidated legislation, Imprensa Nacional-Casa da Moeda)
note: Civil Code (Código Civil), consolidated text, urban lease provisions (Arts. 1064-1113); text in Portuguese, the summary is ours.

value: A fixed term may not be shorter than one year nor longer than 30 years (automatically adjusted to those limits); the minimum does not apply to non-permanent housing or special transitional purposes (Art. 1095). A fixed-term contract renews automatically for equal periods, or three years if shorter, unless otherwise agreed (Art. 1096).
source_publisher: Diário da República (consolidated legislation, Imprensa Nacional-Casa da Moeda)
note: Civil Code (Código Civil), consolidated text, urban lease provisions (Arts. 1064-1113); text in Portuguese, the summary is ours.

value: Payment of rent in advance, if agreed in writing, may not exceed two months; the parties may secure performance by any legally provided form up to the value of two months' rent (Art. 1076).
source_publisher: Diário da República (consolidated legislation, Imprensa Nacional-Casa da Moeda)
note: Civil Code (Código Civil), consolidated text, urban lease provisions (Arts. 1064-1113); text in Portuguese, the summary is ours.

value: If the contract has no written update clause: rent may be updated annually using the official coefficients; the first update can be required one year after the start, then one year after each previous update; the landlord must notify in writing at least 30 days ahead with the coefficient and new rent; unused updates can be applied later but not beyond three years (Art. 1077(2)).
source_publisher: Diário da República (consolidated legislation, Imprensa Nacional-Casa da Moeda)
note: Civil Code (Código Civil), consolidated text, urban lease provisions (Arts. 1064-1113); text in Portuguese, the summary is ours.

value: Rent update coefficient for free-rent housing for 2026 is 1.0224 (Aviso n.º 23174/2025/2). The coefficient for 2027 is 1.0256 (Aviso n.º 24199/2026/2). For 2023 the coefficient was capped at 1.02 by Art. 2 of Law 19/2022; for 2024 it was 1.0694.
source_publisher: Portal da Habitação (IHRU, Government of Portugal)
note: The table is published by IHRU on the Portal da Habitação; the 'free-rent' column was read, the column title is 'Habitação renda livre'.

value: The tenant can prevent automatic renewal by notice at least 120 days (term of 6 years or more), 90 days (1 to under 6 years), 60 days (6 months to under 1 year) before the end of the term (Art. 1098(1)).
source_publisher: Diário da República (consolidated legislation, Imprensa Nacional-Casa da Moeda)
note: Civil Code (Código Civil), consolidated text, urban lease provisions (Arts. 1064-1113); text in Portuguese, the summary is ours.

value: After six months of effective duration the tenant may terminate an indefinite-term lease without reason by notice of 120 days if it has lasted one year or more, or 60 days if up to one year (Art. 1100(1)).
source_publisher: Diário da República (consolidated legislation, Imprensa Nacional-Casa da Moeda)
note: Civil Code (Código Civil), consolidated text, urban lease provisions (Arts. 1064-1113); text in Portuguese, the summary is ours.

value: The landlord may terminate an indefinite-term lease for own or first-degree descendants' housing need, for demolition or deep renovation, or by notice at least five years before the intended end (Art. 1101).
